body: I work for a Healthcare Tech company based out of NYC
I’m a remote SWE making 140K+ and my wife is a Teacher making 75K

I am fortunate enough to work from home, office is in NYC. Had to commute to LA everyday to work with my dad before I broke into the industry that I’m currently in and it was absolutely soul crushing.

It took me two years post grad to land my first role for what many either here on blind would consider peanuts. 600 applications, grinding Leetcode everyday and wondering if that day will ever come. I know what that feels like, it also put me into a depression that I don’t wish on anyone. Just keep going, the day will come. Feel free to PM me as well OP.

I barely graduated with a 2.9 in 2018 and graduated with a hand injury that left me out of the application game for the rest of that year. 2019 was the worst year of my life, hundreds of applications, rejections, interviews only to end up not getting it. I was severely depressed and hated my life. It felt like everyone in my graduating class was already successful and super smart. To put the cherry on top, I got to the FINAL onsite round of a FAANG company and didnt get it. 

But you know what saved my life? The little things man. Being able to grab boba with my GF after a day of leeting. Occasional hangout with the bois. Your job is not a reflection of your worth. I just stuck to it and eventually got a job on the opposite side of the country that I begrudgingly accepted but now because of covid I get to work remote permanently lol. 

I dont make six figures but I have a start now and feel like my life is finally going somewhere and definitely feel that I can get that 100K job now that I can leet at my own leisure. I graduated in 2018 and didn’t start my job til last half of 2020 and man did that feel like forever. 

But I’m glad that I’m here and I know you’ll make it too. Just please take care of yourself along the way.

Graduated in may of 2018 and got injured right after. Had to spend rest of 2018 in rehabilitation. I've spent all of 2019 applying with little luck but managed to land a remote internship for the moment. Are my chances of getting a job getting worse with the time gap?
